chunks.arabic_text: أَبِي رَحِمَهُ ٱللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِدْرِيسَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ ٱبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ يَرْفَعُهُ إِلَى أَحَدِهِمْ ع أَنَّهُ قَالَ

translations.en: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me from Ibn Abi Umair, who raised it to one of them (peace be upon him), that he said:

chunks.arabic_text: بَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ صَلاَةً مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَ بَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ حَجّاً مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَ بَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ صَدَقَةً مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَ بَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ صِيَاماً مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَ أَفْضَلُكُمْ أَفْضَلُ مَعْرِفَةً

translations.en: Some of you offer more prayers than others, and some of you perform more hajj than others, and some of you give more charity than others, and fasting than others. But the best of you is the one with the most knowledge.

en.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Al-Saduq uses this hadith to define the essential Shia identity, asserting that *ma'rifah* (gnostic knowledge of the Imams and divine reality) supersedes the quantitative accumulation of rituals like prayer and fasting. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam as the source of true knowledge, positioning intellectual and spiritual insight as the prerequisite for the validity and excellence of outward acts of worship.
en.seo_question: What is the highest virtue in Shia Islam according to the hadith of the Imams?
